[Read from: /home/tupi/code/Onscreen-Translator/plan.md, /home/tupi/code/Onscreen-Translator/progress.md]

Thoroughly review the OnscreenTranslator.Core library code. Focus on:
1. Interface design (IOCRProvider, ITranslationProvider, IPlatformServices) — are the abstractions clean, future-proof, and platform-agnostic?
2. Provider implementations — correctness, error handling, threading/async issues, HttpClient lifecycle
3. RemoteOCRProvider and RemoteTranslationProvider — security concerns, proper URL handling, auth
4. AppSettings design — JSON serialization, ProtectedStringConverter cross-platform fallback, RemoteServerConfig
5. ProviderFactory — extensibility, the new 'remote' case, switch completeness
6. FuriganaServiceManager — process lifecycle, error recovery, the async fix that was applied
7. Platform/IPlatformServices.cs — is the abstraction sufficient for Windows and Linux?

Flag bugs, design flaws, missing edge cases, and suggest concrete fixes. Be critical.

childReport.diffSummary: Review of the Core library extraction commit (dadcb37) — 38 new files moving shared providers, interfaces, settings, and services into OnscreenTranslator.Core
reviewFindings: blocker: DictionaryLookup.cs:17-23 — sync-over-async (.Wait()/.Result) will deadlock on UI threads
blocker: ProviderFactory.cs:18 — AvailableTranslationProviders missing 'remote' despite DisplayNames and CreateTranslationProvider handling it
blocker: RemoteOCRProvider.cs:46-54 — IsAvailableAsync is a no-op (always returns true), same for RemoteTranslationProvider.cs:52-60
blocker: FuriganaServiceManager.cs:335 — async void OnProcessExited with unguarded await IsHealthyAsync can crash process
major: Providers (all) — each creates own HttpClient (10 instances total), anti-pattern causing socket exhaustion
major: AppSettings.cs:110-117 — encryption failure silently stores API keys as plaintext
major: AppSettings.cs:113-118 — XOR fallback with hardcoded key is not real encryption
major: DeepLTranslationProvider.cs:27 — CancellationToken not passed to TranslateTextAsync
major: OllamaOCRProvider.cs:205 + OpenAIOCRProvider.cs:182 — duplicated CleanOcrOutput (~60 lines each)
major: ProviderFactory.cs:78-82 — CreateOcrProvider default silently falls back to Ollama instead of throwing
major: ProviderFactory.cs:78-110 — CreateTranslationProviders (plural) doesn't include RemoteTranslationProvider
major: OpenAIOCRProvider.cs:48-53 — BaseUrl setter mutates HttpClient.BaseAddress after creation (thread-unsafe)
childReport.manualNotes: The codebase is well-structured overall — the Core extraction is clean, interfaces are properly designed, and FuriganaServiceManager is notably well-engineered. The main risk areas are (1) missing test coverage, (2) HttpClient lifecycle, (3) the security model for API key storage, and (4) the sync-over-async in DictionaryLookup. None are regressions from the extraction — they pre-exist and should be tracked as tech debt.
